title: Imperial Chess Game
next_chapter_hook: When Su Qingyao opened the gilt-edged confidential letter from the imperial city, her fingers trembled slightly—three days later, the Crown Prince's Birthday Banquet.

text.content: As the phantom of the altar dissolved before Chen Ji's eyes, the figure bound by chains seared itself into his soul like a branding iron. The ancient runes surrounding the scene emanated a cold, eerie glow, each pattern seeming to devour something—his sister Chen Nian was being consumed as some kind of sacrifice in a way he could not comprehend. "Chen Nian..." he murmured, fists unconsciously clenching. The agitation of the Tianji Record Fragment had not yet fully subsided; Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul sighed faintly from the first page: "The Tianji Record's foresight never lies, but the existence of the key makes the images blurry. What you saw is merely the tip of the iceberg—the true cage lies buried beneath the imperial city." Beneath the imperial city. These four words darkened Chen Ji's gaze; he suddenly realized that his sister's prison was inextricably linked to the current imperial power.

In the backyard of the Tianqing Sect Servants' Quarters, Chen Ji sat alone in a dilapidated wooden hut, twilight deepening outside the window. The undercurrents of the imperial court had already begun to surge—this was evident from the sudden influx of unfamiliar faces within the sect lately. The Crown Prince Faction's power was at its zenith, while the Princess faction, though weaker, had never abandoned its coveting of power. Chen Ji tucked the Tianji Record Fragment into his sleeve, his expressioncalm得近乎cold. That the Crown Prince and Princess would both seek to approach Su Qingyao was within Chen Ji's expectations—after all, in the official narrative of the Tianqing Sect, Chen Ji was already a "trash弟子" who had "died in the Ancient Forbidden Land," and his remaining "legacy" naturally became juicy prey in the eyes of various forces. How absurd. Chen Ji's lips curved slightly upward, but there was no笑意 in his eyes. He did not mind being treated as dead; what truly concerned him was—why were the imperial forces so desperate to obtain everything he had touched in life? Mo Xiansheng's words echoed in his ears: "When you become part of the chess game, the most dangerous thing is not the chess player, but the other pieces."

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao, Inner Sect Senior Fellow of Tianqing Sect, her identity as "Chen Ji's widow" had recently made her the most sought-after person in the sect. At this moment she sat upright in the center of the Inner Sect Council Hall, her expression characteristically cold. A middle-aged man in dark purple brocade robes sat across from her, the four-clawed python embroidered on his splendid attire gleaming with hidden gold under the candlelight—that was a unique symbol of the Crown Prince's Manor. "Miss Su, although Chen Ji has perished, the Crown Prince has heard that he had a deep fusion with the Tianji Record Fragment before his death." The man was named Wei Zhongxian, chief advisor of the Crown Prince's Manor, his gaze sharp as a hawk's as he spoke. "His Highness, considering Chen Ji's past contributions to the Tianqing Sect, is willing to provide庇护 for Chen Ji's widow in the Crown Prince's name. Of course, the Crown Prince's Manor also hopes that Miss Su will hand over all of Chen Ji's生前遗物, so that the court may... study them." He intentionally emphasized the word "study," a confident smile curling on his lips.

Su Qingyao lifted her tea cup, her slender white fingers tracing gently along the rim, movements elegant yet distant. "Official Wei, Chen Ji was merely a servant disciple before his death—what legacy could he possibly have? As for the Tianji Record—" she raised her eyes, her gaze cold as ice blades sweeping across Wei Zhongxian, "such divine objects, how could an Inner Sect disciple like me possibly have access to?" Wei Zhongxian's smile froze for a moment, then quickly returned to normal: "Miss Su need not be so modest? Everyone in the entire Tianqing Sect knows of Chen Ji's close relationship with you before his death. I'm sure Miss Su can sense His Highness's sincerity." He clapped his hands lightly, and immediately servants outside brought in three sandalwood trunks. As the lids opened, jewels filled the entire room—gold, silver, spirit stones, elixirs, even a lower-grade spirit weapon-level protective soft armor. "This is His Highness's welcoming gift. If Miss Su is willing to frequently engage with the Crown Prince's Manor in the future, the benefits will far exceed this." Wei Zhongxian narrowed his eyes. "Of course, if Miss Su refuses to see reason... the Tianqing Sect's situation may become somewhat precarious." This was naked threat.

text.content: Thirty zhang outside the Council Hall, on an ancient pine tree, Chen Ji concealed himself within the dense branches. The evening breeze brushed past, pine waves surged like tides, yet they could not mask a single word of conversation from within. He saw Wei Zhongxian's smug expression, saw the jeweled light reflecting on Su Qingyao's cold face, saw those spirit stones and weapons displayed before her like alms given to a beggar. The arrogance and greed of the Crown Prince Faction were laid bare before his eyes. But Chen Ji did not move. His fingers gently stroked the Tianji Record Fragment in his sleeve, his mind racing. Wei Zhongxian's appearance confirmed his previous speculation—the imperial city's interest in the Tianji Record was far more urgent than he had imagined. Amid the friction between the three major sects, the imperial court should have stayed out of it, yet now they were so eager to intervene—what did this mean? The answer was only one—the Tianji Record was no ordinary cultivation secret treasure; it had some deeper connection to the foundation of imperial power.

dialogue.content: The moment Wei Zhongxian's threatening words fell, the side door of the Council Hall was gently knocked. A maidservant in plain robes walked in with her head lowered, holding an unremarkable bamboo tube. "Miss Su, this was sent to be delivered to you just now, said to be... something from an old friend." Su Qingyao took the bamboo tube, from which she extracted a small jade pendant. The pendant was pure white throughout, the front carved with a spreading blue phoenix, the back bearing only four characters—"Changle Weiyang." Wei Zhongxian's expression instantly darkened; he rose abruptly, his gaze on that jade pendant almost spitting fire. "The Changle Princess's Manor token!" he hissed, "Who? Who dares to play such tricks before this official!" Su Qingyao tucked the jade pendant into her sleeve, her expression still indifferent: "Official Wei, why must you be so agitated? A gift from an old friend—what does that have to do with the Crown Prince's Manor?" This sentence concealed needles in silk; Wei Zhongxian's face turned livid with rage, yet he had no way to vent his fury.

text.content: Chen Ji observed everything clearly from atop the ancient pine. The appearance of the Changle Princess's Manor token was so precise, as if it had been waiting in the shadows for the Crown Prince Faction to bare its fangs. He closed his eyes; the Tianji Record Fragment in his sleeve grew slightly warm—this was his deliberate doing. Three days ago, he had used the Tianji Record to foresee today's scene, including when Wei Zhongxian would arrive, what words he would speak, how Su Qingyao would respond, and... when the Changle Princess's envoy would appear. He had even foreseen what would be carved on that jade pendant. The cost was fifteen points of Heavenly Fate. Chen Ji opened his eyes, his gaze profound as an abyss. The Crown Prince and Princess—two completely different paths lay before him. The Crown Prince's Manor represented current legitimacy, possessing overwhelming resources and military strength, but precisely because of this, partners would only become pieces on the chessboard that could be discarded at any moment. As for the Changle Princess—Chen Ji recalled rumors about this person; though she was a woman, she harbored great strategies, had cultivated her network in court for years, secretly controlling an intelligence network unknown to others. Most importantly, she was the only member of the royal family who showed interest in "variables" outside the three major sects.

choice.prompt: The Crown Prince's Manor was powerful, the Princess's Manor was weak, but what Chen Ji needed was never the strongest backing, but the chessboard that best allowed him to hide in the shadows. Both paths had advantages and disadvantages—aligning with the Crown Prince meant resources and protection, but also complete exposure at the heart of imperial power, one misstep meaning utter destruction; aligning with the Princess carried smaller risks, but whether the Princess's ambitions aligned with his own remained unknown. And that thought of "remaining neutral"—Chen Ji himself could not tell if it was deep deliberation or some deeper layer of scheming...

choices.text: Secretly Ally with the Crown Prince
choices.description: The Crown Prince's Manor possesses overwhelming resources and legitimacy; aligning with them provides maximum protection, but also means complete exposure at the heart of imperial power.
choices.visible_cost: Losing the initiative forscheme in secret
choices.visible_reward: Gaining the Crown Prince's Manor resource protection
choices.risk_hint: The Crown Prince Faction has already regarded you as exploitable legacy

text.content: Chen Ji silently dropped from the ancient pine, his landing light and swift as a specter. He did not act immediately; instead, he quickly formulated a plan in his mind to contact the Crown Prince Faction—as "an old friend of Chen Ji before his death." What the Crown Prince's Manor sought was the secret of the Tianji Record; since that was the case, he might as well give them a taste, exchanging it for the opportunity to delve deeper into the imperial city. After all, to reach the depths beneath the imperial city, the Crown Prince's Manor's connections might be the fastest route. "Wei Zhongxian..." he murmured the name, a cold glint flickering in his eyes, "noted."

choices.description: Although the Changle Princess's Manor is weak, it is the only royal faction interested in "variables"; allying with them carries smaller risks and better aligns with the principle ofscheme in secret.
choices.visible_cost: Extremely limited initial resources and manpower
choices.visible_reward: Preserving maximum initiative forscheme in secret
choices.risk_hint: The direction of the Princess's ambitions remains unclear

text.content: Chen Ji chose the path more consistent with his usual style. He took out a transmission talisman from his chest, already prepared, and used his finger as a pen to swiftly write several lines on the talisman paper—"The fragment is undestroyed, the opportunity remains. Beneath the imperial city, something answers heaven." Sixteen brief characters, sufficient to arouse all of the Changle Princess's curiosity. He folded the talisman into a paper crane, infused it with spiritual energy, and released it. In the night, that paper crane turned into a streak of light, disappearing toward the imperial city. Chen Ji's lips curved slightly: "Princess, since you are interested in the legacy of the 'dead,' let us see who is the true hunter in this game."

choices.description: Choose neither faction, continue observing from the shadows in the identity of a dead person, waiting for a better opportunity to介入 the Imperial Chess Game.
choices.visible_cost: Temporarily abandon the opportunity to leverage imperial power
choices.visible_reward: Maintain the utmost concealment and freedom
choices.risk_hint: The imperial dynasty will not give you endless time to observe

text.content: Chen Ji withdrew the paper crane into his sleeve, making the choice he was best at—biding his time. The confrontation between the Prince's Manor and the Princess's Manor had just begun; both sides needed time to probe each other's bottom lines and chips, while he only needed to continue being a 'dead man'. He turned and merged into the night, his form dissolving into the shadows of the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul whispered from within his sleeve: 'Those who choose neutrality are often the last to clean up the aftermath. You are becoming more and more like your father.' Chen Ji's footsteps hesitated slightly, then continued forward. Father... that question, he didn't want to touch for now.

Su Qingyao used tea as wine in the Inner Sect Council Hall, gracefully yet firmly seeing off Wei Zhongxian. The three boxes of jewels and treasures she refused to touch, ordering them all sent back to the Prince's temporary residence in the sect. Wei Zhongxian's expression as he left was quite a sight—first stunned, then furious, finally dissolving into a cold, sinister smile. He spoke no threats, but that 'we'll see' undertone chilled the air in the council hall by several degrees. Su Qingyao sat alone in the empty hall, the candlelight illuminating her cold, serene profile. She drew out the jade pendant from the Princess of Changle's manor from her sleeve, turning it between her fingers, a faint smile playing at her lips. 'Chen Ji ah Chen Ji, you thought you died so well?' she murmured to herself, her voice revealing neither hatred nor longing, 'These messes you left behind—now I have to clean them up.'

dialogue.content: The night deepened. Su Qingyao sat alone in her chambers, an urgent secret letter spread before her. The letter was made of imperial golden silk paper, and the wax seal bore an imprint of a soaring cyan phoenix—the crest of the Princess of Changle's manor. She broke the seal, and familiar elegant calligraphy met her eyes: 'To Miss Su: Hearing of your recent troubles, this palace feels deeply for you. Though Chen Ji has passed, his legacy lives on. The secrets of the Tianji Record concern all under heaven; they cannot be solved by one party alone. In three days, the Crown Prince's birthday banquet—this palace will host a small gathering, hoping to converse with you then. A Qingluan envoy will welcome you, hoping you will honor us with your presence. Burn this letter after reading, to avoid complications.' At the letter's end, a small note was attached: 'If he knew you were well in the netherworld, he would surely be at peace.' Su Qingyao's hand trembled slightly; that line seemed to carry a certain warmth, piercing through the cold shell she had so carefully constructed over time. She stared at those words for a long while, finally holding the letter to the candle flame, watching the golden silk paper turn to ash inch by inch.

text.content: Meanwhile, in a deep palace hall within the imperial city's Grand Interior. Princess of Changle Li Changning reclined on a cushioned couch, toying with a jade pendant identical to Su Qingyao's. Rare aloeswood incense burned in the hall, wisps of blue smoke swirling in the candlelight, yet failing to dispel the heavy gloom between her brows. 'Your Highness, news has come from the Crown Prince's side—Wei Zhongxian hit a snag at the Tianqing Sect.' A low voice emerged from the shadows. 'That Miss Su not only rejected the Crown Prince faction's recruitment but also returned all three boxes of gifts untouched.' Li Changning's lips curved slightly: 'She's got spirit. No wonder Chen Ji looked upon her with special regard.' She tucked the jade pendant into her sleeve, rose, and walked toward the window. The ten thousand lights of the imperial city spread out before her eyes, like an unfinished game of chess. 'Issue the order—three days from now at the birthday banquet, this princess will meet this Miss Su personally. And—' her voice turned icy, 'Find out, did Chen Ji truly die? What this palace wants is no 'widow'—I want a living chess piece.'

choice.prompt: Chen Ji observed all of this from the shadows. The Crown Prince's greed, the Princess's scheming, Su Qingyao's maneuvering—the full picture of the imperial game's confrontation was unfolding before him. Yet the secret letter Su Qingyao received meant she was about to be drawn into this vortex of power. Chen Ji had to make a choice: continue to observe as a 'secret guardian', or personally intervene to pull Su Qingyao out from between the two forces? Or—make her a bright chess piece in his own scheme?

choices.description: Use a shadow identity to establish protection around Su Qingyao, preventing her from being caught in any faction's grip.
choices.visible_cost: Risking exposure of the fact that he is still alive
choices.visible_reward: Ensuring Su Qingyao's safety and freedom

dialogue.content: Chen Ji emerged silently from the shadows. He startled no one, merely laying an extremely hidden perception array outside Su Qingyao's chambers. This formation used the aura of the Tianji Record Fragment as its guide, capable of sending him a warning whenever anyone approached Su Qingyao. He stepped back, gazing at the thin silhouette on the window paper, and whispered: 'Su Qingyao, you may hate me, but you must stay alive.' His voice was so low even the wind could not hear it.

choices.text: Make her a bright chess piece
choices.description: Utilize the opportunity of the Crown Prince's birthday banquet to have Su Qingyao serve as a double agent under the identity of 'Chen Ji's widow', navigating between the two powers.
choices.visible_cost: Su Qingyao will bear tremendous risk
choices.visible_reward: Gain an intelligence line running through the heart of the imperial dynasty
choices.risk_hint: Once exposed, Su Qingyao will become the target of all parties

text.content: Chen Ji returned to his hiding place, took out the Tianji Record Fragment, and carved a series of runes only he could read onto it. These runes would automatically activate at specific moments, transmitting his carefully designed intelligence commands to Su Qingyao. He tucked the fragment into his chest, his eyes ice-cold. 'Su Qingyao, haven't you always wanted to know what kind of person I am?' he murmured to himself, 'Then let you walk in and see for yourself.' This was a gamble, with her trust as the stakes, and he had always been willing to play.

choices.description: No longer hide, but appear before Su Qingyao in a 'resurrected' form before the Crown Prince's birthday banquet, meeting her withcandid
choices.visible_cost: Completely abandon the advantages of the 'dead man' identity
choices.visible_reward: Establish a true alliance with Su Qingyao
choices.risk_hint: All secret schemes will be re-examined

dialogue.content: Chen Ji removed his outer robe, revealing the face the world believed had rotted away in the Forbidden Grounds. He adjusted his appearance before a bronze mirror, his movements unhurried, as if merely heading to an ordinary appointment. 'Su Qingyao, three times now—three times you've come infinitely close to the truth.' he said softly, a complex curve forming at the corner of his lips. 'The fourth time, let me tell you the answer myself.' Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul sighed within the Tianji Record: 'Are you certain? Once she knows you're still alive, everything will change.' Chen Ji gave no answer. He had already stepped out into the night.

text.content: Night wind swept through the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain, carrying a biting chill. Chen Ji sat cross-legged on a massive boulder at the mountain summit, the Tianji Record Fragment spread open before him. On the fragment, a blurry image was slowly taking shape—the Crown Prince's birthday banquet three days hence. In the vision, the magnificent palace was adorned with lanterns and decorations, guests crowding like clouds. Su Qingyao stood among the crowd in a plain white gown, remarkably conspicuous. And at the highest point of the palace, the current Crown Prince surveyed everything from above, a playful smile hanging at the corner of his lips. The image continued shifting, passing through corridors, crossing courtyards, finally freezing on a bronze gate deep within the palace—on the other side lay bottomless darkness and the faint sound of chains. Chen Nian. Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply. The Tianji Record Fragment trembled violently, the image blurring once more, but that fleeting glimpse was enough for him to confirm—his sister Chen Nian was within the imperial capital where the Crown Prince's birthday banquet would be held, just three days' journey away.

Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul drifted slowly from the first page of the Tianji Record, transforming into a faint glow that floated at Chen Ji's side. "Did you see it? Beneath the imperial capital, the altar lies right beneath the banquet." The old man's voice was aged and weary. "The Crown Prince may not know what is buried beneath his feet, but Princess Changle... she certainly does." Chen Ji silently put away the Tianji Record Fragment, raising his head to gaze toward the imperial capital. There, ten thousand household lights blazed brilliantly, like a burning golden mountain, each lamp concealing a scheme he had yet to see through. The Crown Prince's Manor was set on victory, the Princess's Manor was scheming in the shadows, Su Qingyao was caught in the vortex, and his sister was bound by chains in the deepest darkness of the imperial capital. The Crown Prince's birthday banquet three days hence would inevitably become the stage where various forces made their formal appearances. And he, Chen Ji, a supposedly dead talentless disciple, was about to return to the center of this game in some manner. Mo Xiansheng's glow gradually faded, leaving behind only a profoundly meaningful sigh: "The chessboard of fate has been set; now, it's your turn to make a move."

The Inner Disciple dormitory district of the Tianqing Sect, night had deepened. Su Qingyao sat before the window, repeatedly tracing the spot where the letter had been reduced to ashes. Candlelight flickered, casting her lonely silhouette on the wall. The Crown Prince's birthday banquet three days hence, whether she wished it or not, had already dragged her into the vortex of this imperial game. The Crown Prince faction's threats still echoed in her ears, the Princess faction's olive branch had already been extended, yet the shadow of that "dead man" in her heart refused to dissipate. "Chen Ji..." she murmured softly, gripping the jade token in her hand tightly—this was the token of Princess Changle's Manor, and also the only trump card she had yet to play. What she didn't know was that, three zhang away from her dormitory window in the shadows, a pair of eyes was silently watching that cold silhouette on the window paper. Chen Ji withdrew his gaze, his form melting into the depths of night. The Tianji Record Fragment in his sleeve emitted faint warmth—a feedback from the Heavenly Fate Value consumed by its final warning, and also a silent reminder: the countdown of fate has already begun.
